recognize_zh: HPLC 圖上 4.09 分鐘（D-window，43.6%）與 4.36 分鐘（S-window，33.8%）兩個相鄰的高峰形成「雙峰」，HbA 幾乎消失（Ao 2.0%），HbF 升高到 12.6%；同時出現 S 與 D 變異且無 HbA，符合 HbS/HbD-Punjab 雙重異合子（HbSD disease）。
features: Cation-exchange HPLC report with peak table and chromatogram (lower-resolution scan)
Two large closely spaced variant peaks: D-window at 4.09 min (43.6%) and S-window at 4.36 min (33.8%)
Raised HbF at 12.6% (1.12 min) and HbA2 3.5%
Several small unknown peaks between 1.9 and 2.9 min
describe_en: Cation-exchange HPLC shows two large adjacent variant peaks, one in the D-window at 4.09 minutes (43.6%) and one in the S-window at 4.36 minutes (33.8%), with near-absence of HbA (2.0%). HbF is increased at 12.6% and HbA2 is 3.5%. The co-existence of D- and S-window variants without significant HbA indicates compound heterozygosity for HbS and a D-window variant, most likely HbD-Punjab, confirmed by parental studies showing HbS trait and HbD trait. Findings are consistent with HbSD disease, a clinically significant sickling disorder.

ddx.vs: HbSS shows a single S-window peak without a separate D-window peak.

ddx.dx: HbS trait with a split or degraded S peak
ddx.vs: Sample aging can create shoulder peaks, but HbS trait retains more HbA than HbS, whereas here HbA is almost absent.
HbG-Philadelphia is an alpha-chain variant producing hybrid peaks with retained HbA and is non-sickling in combination, so DNA sequencing is needed to identify the D-window variant definitively.
